course.title: Statistics I: Probability and Descriptive Statistics
course.description: This course is designed to provide students with knowledge related to statistics and probability. Students will learn how to collect, summarize, visualize data, apply probability concepts, and perform basic statistical analyses. The tasks will include questionnaire design, sampling technique, data collection, data entry, data management, data summary, graphical display, descriptive statistics (central tendency and variability), variable correlation, regression analysis, probability distribution, confidence interval, and hands-on statistical software practice.

contentRows: Topic 1: Introduction to statistics and data types Lab 1: Introduction to SPSS interface, data types, measurement scales, and importing data
Topic 2: Questionnaire Design and Variables Lab 2: Questionnaire design and variable coding in SPSS
Topic 3: Data Collection and Sampling Techniques Lab 3: Data entry, editing, and validation in SPSS
Topic 4: Graphical Methods for Describing Data Lab 4: Graphical display (bar charts, pie charts, and histograms) by SPSS
Topic 5: Numerical Methods for Describing Data (Central tendency) Lab 5: Descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode) by SPSS
Topic 6: Numerical Methods for Describing Data (Dispersion) Lab 6: Descriptive statistics (variance, standard deviation, range, IQR, boxplots) by SPSS
Topic 7: Correlation analysis Lab 7: Pearson correlation by SPSS
Topic 8: Simple Linear Regression Lab 8: Simple regression analysis by SPSS and interpretation
Topic 9: Random Variables and Probability Distributions Lab 9: Data cleaning (missing values and outlier detection), and the procedure for replacing missing values by SPSS
Topic 10: Random Variables Mean and Standard Deviation Lab 10: Computing new variables and data transformation by SPSS
Topic 11: Normal Distributions and Transforming Normality Lab 11: Normality testing and Z-score calculations
Topic 12: Sampling Variability and Sampling Distributions Lab 12: Transforming normality by SPSS
Topic 13: Confidence Interval for Binomial Probability Lab 13: Construct and interpret confidence intervals by SPSS
Topic 14: Confidence Interval for Population Mean Lab 14: Construct and interpret confidence intervals by SPSS

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to statistics and data types Lab 1: Introduction to SPSS interface, data types, measurement scales, and importing data
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain the role of statistics in data science and engineering applications. Lecture: Classify different types of data and measurement scales used in statistical analysis. Lab: Identify data types and measurement scales and correctly import datasets into SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 2: Questionnaire Design and Variables Lab 2: Questionnaire design and variable coding in SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Design structured questionnaires and define variables suitable for statistical analysis. Lab: Create questionnaires and perform variable coding accurately using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 3: Data Collection and Sampling Techniques Lab 3: Data entry, editing, and validation in SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain common data collection methods and sampling techniques used in statistical studies. Lab: Enter, edit, and validate collected data correctly using SPSS tools.

topics.title: Topic 4: Graphical Methods for Describing Data Lab 4: Graphical display (bar charts, pie charts, and histograms) by SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Select appropriate graphical methods to represent different types of data. Lab: Construct and interpret bar charts, pie charts, and histograms using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 5: Numerical Methods for Describing Data (Central tendency) Lab 5: Descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode) by SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain measures of central tendency and their interpretation in real datasets. Lab: Compute and interpret mean, median, and mode using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 6: Numerical Methods for Describing Data (Dispersion) Lab 6: Descriptive statistics (variance, standard deviation, range, IQR, boxplots) by SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain measures of data dispersion and variability. Lab: Calculate and interpret variance, standard deviation, range, IQR, and boxplots using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 7: Correlation analysis Lab 7: Pearson correlation by SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain the concept of correlation and its role in identifying relationships between variables. Lab: Perform Pearson correlation analysis and interpret results using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 8: Simple Linear Regression Lab 8: Simple regression analysis by SPSS and interpretation
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain the principles and assumptions of simple linear regression. Lab: Conduct simple linear regression analysis and interpret regression outputs using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 9: Random Variables and Probability Distributions Lab 9: Data cleaning (missing values and outlier detection), and the procedure for replacing missing values by SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain the concepts of random variables and common probability distributions. Lab: Detect missing values and outliers and apply appropriate data cleaning procedures using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 10: Random Variables Mean and Standard Deviation Lab 10: Computing new variables and data transformation by SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain the mean and standard deviation of random variables and their interpretations. Lab: Compute new variables and perform data transformation using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 11: Normal Distributions and Transforming Normality Lab 11: Normality testing and Z-score calculations
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain the properties of the normal distribution and the concept of normality. Lab: Conduct normality tests and compute Z-scores using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 12: Sampling Variability and Sampling Distributions Lab 12: Transforming normality by SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain sampling variability and the concept of sampling distributions. Lab: Apply data transformation techniques to improve normality using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 13: Confidence Interval for Binomial Probability Lab 13: Construct and interpret confidence intervals by SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain the concept and interpretation of confidence intervals for binomial proportions. Lab: Construct and interpret confidence intervals for binomial probability using SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 14: Confidence Interval for Population Mean Lab 14: Construct and interpret confidence intervals by SPSS
topics.llosRaw: Lecture: Explain the construction and interpretation of confidence intervals for population means. Lab: Construct and interpret confidence intervals for population means using SPSS.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
